summary: Approve. The integer-first BigInt conversion fixes the reported precision loss while preserving fractional rounding and overflow handling. All 46 Duration tests passed; a plain-node probe verified exact conversion, signed hrtime output, equality, hashing, and HashSet lookup across large values. Reported two non-blocking test-coverage nits; no correctness defects found. Broad check/lint runs were intentionally omitted as requested.

params.title: Extend the large-millis regression to equality and hashing
params.body: The new assertion covers conversion, but the PR also promises that mixed Millis/Nanos equality and hashing use the corrected canonical value. Consider adding this epoch-sized value to the existing hash/equality test, including a HashSet lookup against Duration.nanos(1_760_450_000_123_000_000n). The existing cases use small milliseconds or overflow-sized values, both of which already worked before this patch. This is a non-blocking coverage suggestion, not an observed implementation defect.

params.title: Cover the motivating hrtime example and its negative counterpart
params.body: Consider asserting toHrTime for the epoch-sized value as well as its negative counterpart: [1760450000, 123000000] and [-1760450000, -123000000]. The description explicitly cites this conversion, but the existing toHrTime test only exercises small positive durations. This would retain coverage of exact remainder extraction and signed output at the magnitude addressed here; the implementation currently behaves correctly.

params.title: Cover the motivating hrtime example and its negative counterpart
params.body: Consider adding toHrTime assertions for the epoch-sized value and its negative counterpart: [1760450000, 123000000] and [-1760450000, -123000000]. The description explicitly cites this conversion through the changed helper, but the existing toHrTime test only exercises small positive durations. This would preserve coverage of exact remainder extraction and signed output at the magnitude addressed here. This is non-blocking: the implementation currently behaves correctly.

Validation: pnpm test --run packages/effect/test/Duration.test.ts passed all 46 tests. A temporary scratchpad script run with plain node confirmed exact nanoseconds, mixed-representation equality, identical hashes, and HashSet lookup for ±1_760_450_000_123, Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, and ±2 ** 1023. No defect reproduced; the suggestion is to preserve those checks in the suite.

The plain-node scratchpad probe returned exactly [1760450000, 123000000] and [-1760450000, -123000000]. Fractional ties still rounded to ±2n for ±0.0000015 ms, and NaN/infinity/negative-zero normalization was unchanged. All 46 Duration tests passed. The temporary probe was removed and git status is clean.
